data_quality_gate.disclosure: The defect was found during error analysis of the earlier test evaluation. The gate is the pre-existing runtime rule and was not tuned on test data; the threshold was re-selected on validation only and the test set was scored once afterwards.
data_quality_gate.reason: The original extraction accepted any single detected face; in crowded scenes this was sometimes a ~20 px background bystander instead of the subject.
data_quality_gate.rule: faceguard.pipeline.face_quality_reason with the unchanged configs/runtime.yaml thresholds (detection >= 0.6, face side >= 80 px, brightness 40-215, Laplacian variance >= 40)

limitations: Exploratory unknown-session split; not an official benchmark.
Confidence intervals resample person identities, but sessions/devices are unknown.
Known-person probes come from the same capture sitting as enrollment (202 of 205 identities with timestamped filenames were photographed within 5 minutes); this is not a cross-session result.
Identity pairs 0178/0231 and 0191/0218 appear to be the same people filed under two IDs (embedding similarity and visual check); labels were not changed.

impostor_zero_event_upper_bound_95.method: exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson (approximately the rule of three, 3/n)
impostor_zero_event_upper_bound_95.note: 0/259 false accepts bounds the rate below 1.15% at 95% confidence assuming independent searches; searches come from only 23 identities, so this bound is optimistic. The percentile bootstrap interval collapses to [0, 0] when no events occur and must not be read as a guarantee.

score_unit: one gallery search per probe image

superseded_result.note: 16 of the 20 earlier test errors involved bystander-face samples removed by the quality gate.
